stem: How is over- or under-absorbed overhead calculated?

options.content: Overhead absorbed less actual overhead
options.rationale: Correct: a positive result means over-absorbed.

options.content: Actual overhead less budgeted overhead
options.rationale: That compares spending with the budget, not absorption.

options.content: Budgeted overhead less overhead absorbed
options.rationale: Absorption is compared with the actual overhead incurred.

options.content: Actual activity less budgeted activity
options.rationale: That is only one cause of the difference.

explanation: Over- or under-absorption = overhead absorbed - actual overhead. Positive is over-absorbed; negative is under-absorbed.

stem: What does it mean if overhead is under-absorbed?

options.content: The overhead charged to products is less than the overhead actually incurred
options.rationale: Correct: the products have not carried all the cost.

options.content: The overhead charged to products is more than the overhead incurred
options.rationale: That is over-absorption.

options.content: The factory has spent less than its budget
options.rationale: Spending below budget tends to cause over-absorption.

options.content: The absorption rate is calculated from actual figures
options.rationale: The rate is always pre-determined.

explanation: Under-absorption means the absorbed overhead is lower than the actual overhead, so some real cost has not been charged to products.

stem: How is under-absorbed overhead treated in the statement of profit or loss?

options.content: It is added to profit as extra income
options.rationale: That is the treatment of over-absorbed overhead.

options.content: It is deducted from profit as an extra expense
options.rationale: Correct: costs were not fully charged to products.

options.content: It is added to the value of closing inventory
options.rationale: The adjustment is made to profit in the period.

options.content: It is ignored because it is only an estimate
options.rationale: The difference is real cost and must be recorded.

explanation: Under-absorbed overhead is a cost not yet charged, so it is debited to profit or loss and reduces profit.

stem: A factory budgets overheads of US\$84,000 and 14,000 direct labour hours, and absorbs overheads on direct labour hours. Actual overheads were US\$85,500 and 14,650 hours were worked. What was the result?

options.content: US\$2,400 under-absorbed
options.rationale: The amount is right but the direction is wrong: absorbed exceeds actual.

options.content: US\$2,400 over-absorbed
options.rationale: Correct: absorbed 87,900 less actual 85,500.

options.content: US\$1,500 over-absorbed
options.rationale: This is the extra spending compared with the budget.

options.content: US\$1,500 under-absorbed
options.rationale: This compares actual with budget, and ignores the extra hours worked.

hints: Absorbed overhead = actual hours × budgeted rate.

stem: Which situation is most likely to cause overhead to be over-absorbed?

options.content: Activity lower than budget with fixed overheads as budgeted
options.rationale: Fewer hours absorb less, causing under-absorption.

options.content: Actual overheads much higher than budget with activity as budgeted
options.rationale: Higher spending with the same absorption gives under-absorption.

options.content: A rate calculated using actual overheads
options.rationale: The rate is always pre-determined.

options.content: Activity much higher than budget while fixed overheads are as budgeted
options.rationale: Correct: more hours absorb more overhead than planned.

explanation: A high output absorbs more overhead while fixed overheads are unchanged, so absorbed exceeds actual.
hints: Think about what is absorbed and what is spent.

stem: In the production overhead control account, which entry represents the overhead absorbed into products?

options.content: A debit, with the credit in work in progress
options.rationale: Actual overheads are debited; absorbed overhead is credited.

options.content: A credit, with the debit in the bank account
options.rationale: Bank is credited when overheads are paid.

options.content: A credit, with the debit in work in progress
options.rationale: Correct: absorption transfers overhead to the cost of products.

options.content: A debit, with the credit in the statement of profit or loss
options.rationale: Profit or loss receives only the balance of the account.

explanation: Actual overheads are debited to the control account; the overhead absorbed is credited, and the work in progress account is debited.
hints: Actual overheads are debited to the control account.

stem: A bakery under-absorbed overhead although it worked more hours than budgeted. What must have happened?

options.content: The absorption rate was set too high
options.rationale: A higher rate would absorb more, not less.

options.content: Fixed overhead fell as the hours increased
options.rationale: That would help absorption, not reduce it.

options.content: Actual overhead rose by more than the extra absorption
options.rationale: Correct: overspending outweighed the benefit of the extra hours.

options.content: Budgeted hours were never used in the rate
options.rationale: The rate is always based on budgeted hours.

explanation: More hours absorb more overhead. Under-absorption in spite of that means actual spending exceeded the budget by even more.
hints: Extra hours absorb more, so what else changed?

stem: Over-absorbed overhead is added to profit.
explanation: True. Products were charged with more overhead than was incurred, so profit is increased by the adjustment.

stem: Overhead can be over-absorbed even when actual overhead is greater than the budgeted overhead.
explanation: True. If activity is much higher than budget, the extra absorbed can exceed the extra spending.
hints: Consider the effect of high activity.

stem: Match each situation to its result.

left.content: Activity below budget; spending equal to budget
Spending below budget; activity equal to budget

explanation: Absorbed greater than actual is over-absorbed. Low activity absorbs less than planned; low spending leaves absorbed greater than actual.

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: When overhead is under-absorbed, the amount is {{blank:a}} from profit. When it is over-absorbed, the amount is {{blank:b}} to profit.

explanation: Under-absorption reduces profit; over-absorption increases it.

stem: Name the account in which actual overheads are debited and absorbed overheads are credited.
explanation: It is the production overhead control account.

stem: A Harare engineering firm uses a machine hour rate of US\$5.50. In the year 9,800 machine hours were worked and actual overheads were US\$57,200. Calculate the overhead absorbed in the year.
explanation: 9,800 × 5.5 = US\$53,900. The actual overhead (US\$57,200) is the amount incurred, not the amount absorbed.
workedSolution: 1. 9,800 × 5.5 = US\$53,900. The actual overhead (US\$57,200) is the amount incurred, not the amount absorbed.

stem: Using the figures in the previous question, calculate the under-absorbed overhead for the year.
explanation: Absorbed 53,900 - actual 57,200 = (3,300), so US\$3,300 was under-absorbed.
workedSolution: 1. Absorbed 53,900 - actual 57,200 = (3,300), so US\$3,300 was under-absorbed.
hints: Actual less absorbed, when the answer is under-absorbed.

stem: A tailoring workshop absorbs overheads at 120% of direct labour cost. Actual direct labour cost for the year was US\$31,500 and actual overheads were US\$36,150. Calculate the over-absorbed overhead.
hints: Absorbed = 120% of the actual labour cost.

stem: A factory budgeted overheads of US\$160,000 and 20,000 machine hours. Only 18,500 hours were worked. Calculate how much less overhead was absorbed because of the lower activity than the budget.
explanation: Rate = 160,000 ÷ 20,000 = US\$8. Shortfall = 1,500 hours × 8 = US\$12,000 less absorbed.
workedSolution: 1. Rate = 160,000 ÷ 20,000 = US\$8. Shortfall = 1,500 hours × 8 = US\$12,000 less absorbed.
hints: Multiply the shortfall in hours by the rate.

stem: Give two reasons why overhead may be under-absorbed in a year.

points.description: Activity was lower than the budgeted activity, so less overhead was absorbed
Actual overheads were higher than the budget (for example higher electricity or rent)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Output may be below the level budgeted, so fewer hours absorb less overhead; or actual overheads may exceed the budget.

explanation: One mark for each reason.

stem: Explain how the under-absorption of overhead affects the profit and the cost of products.

points.description: The overhead absorbed is less than the actual overhead, so products are under-costed
Profit calculated using absorbed costs is overstated
The under-absorbed amount is deducted from profit to correct it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Products carry less overhead than was really incurred, so profit appears higher than it is. The under-absorbed amount is charged to the statement of profit or loss, reducing profit.

explanation: One mark for each point.
hints: Think about what was charged to products and what was actually spent.

stem: A firm has under-absorbed overheads three years in succession. Advise management on what to do.

points.description: Repeated under-absorption suggests that the rate is too low or the budgeted activity is too optimistic
Prices based on the rate have been too low, so profit is lower than it appears
Review and revise the budget and the rate (and the base) using realistic activity
Control spending where actual overheads exceed the budget

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Repeated under-absorption shows that the rate is too low, so prices have been too low. Management should set realistic activity levels, revise the rate and control overhead spending.

explanation: One mark for each point.
hints: Think of the rate, the prices and the budget.

stem: Mutare Pumps Ltd absorbs production overheads on direct labour hours. Its budget for 2026 was overheads of US\$135,000 and 18,000 direct labour hours. Actual results were 16,800 direct labour hours and actual overheads of US\$131,400.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount of overhead that was under-absorbed.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount by which absorption fell short because of the lower activity than budget.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount by which the actual overhead was below the budget.

options.content: It is added to profit
options.rationale: That is over-absorption.

options.content: It is added to inventory
options.rationale: It is charged to the period.

options.content: It is carried forward to the next year
options.rationale: The control account is cleared.

options.content: It is deducted from profit
options.rationale: Correct.

parts.stem: Explain why overhead was under-absorbed even though actual spending was below the budget, and suggest one action.

points.description: The lower activity cost 9,000 of absorption, more than the saving in spending of 3,600
